newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Unaffected by increased stocks.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Unaffected by increased stocks.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market was quiet in thin talks on Thursday and traders expected the slow sentiment to lock prices in a narrow range in the near term.
Singapore's weekly residue stocks, which rose by 1.825 million barrels in the week ending April 9 to 10.054 million barrels, had little impact on the market, traders said.
Stocks for the previous week ending April 2 showed a 2.435 million barrels draw down to an atleast three-year low of 8.229 million barrels.
Some said the high stocks could dampen sentiment slightly with routine cargoes still coming in from the Middle East but most said the data would have little impact.
But others said the rise was expected considering the sharp fall in the previous week.
"The TDB data is just a reference and it does not matter much to the market," said a trader with an independent.
Many traders said they were directionless and expected slow market movements.
On Wednesday, the 380-cst grade was offered at $93.5 per tonne, compared with last week's $92.5 trading level.

Despite tight supplies on the 180-cst grade bunker fuel oil, traders did not see fresh enquiries from the bunker market. "It seems demand from the bunker market did not pick up," said one. Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) said it bought at least two cargoes of low pour fuel oil at $123 and $113 per tonne respectively for May and June deliveries.
Industry sources said CPC bought four cargoes.
In the LSWR market, traders remain bearish due to poor demand from Japan, expecting prices to fall below $15 per barrel.
"I think Japanese companies will only start enquiries in June for summer demand," said a Japanese trader.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
